profiles.heading: Profiles
profiles.note: One profile of each kind, and the named profiles of the passkey policy (chosen by application and group) and of the locale policy (chosen by application) — see their tabs. The list is paged like every list in this console.
profiles.json: The same over JSON is /admin/policies?format=json and GET /admin-api/policies; the actions on this page are
lead: A policy here is a rule this realm holds a credential to. Each kind is a SEPARATE policy with its own entry in its own container and its own tab, and each has a profile — default — which applies to every person in this realm; the passkey policy may also have named profiles, each applying to the applications and groups it names, and the locale policy named profiles applying to the applications it names.
notXacml: . This is not the XACML policy repository:
notXacmlEnd: holds documents a PDP evaluates, in ou=policies.
authn.heading: Authentication policy — the default profile
authn.lead: Which ways of signing in this realm accepts as a FIRST factor and as a SECOND, and when a second factor is required. Asked at every sign-in door, in both modes: this policy decides what the sign-in screen offers, not whether a credential is checked.
authn.noMail: This realm cannot send mail, so the two email mechanisms are drawn disabled below and are never offered. Configure a transport on
authn.fromRealm: This realm's own profile is stored at {dn}. Removing it puts this realm back to the default realm's profile, or to the built-in defaults where the default realm has none.
authn.fromDefaultRealm: This realm has no profile of its own, and follows the default realm's ({dn}). Saving this form writes this realm's own, which overrides it here and nowhere else.
authn.builtIn: Nothing is stored, so the built-in defaults are in force. Saving this form writes cn=default under ou=authnPolicies. Saved in the DEFAULT realm, it is the policy of every realm that has none of its own.
authn.checked: Every field is checked before anything is written. At least one mechanism must be accepted as a first factor, and if a second factor is required of everybody at least one must be accepted as a second. A person who HOLDS a second factor is asked for it whatever this says: there is no setting that skips a held factor.
authn.now: What this realm accepts, right now
authn.dash: A dash is a role the mechanism cannot have: an authenticator app or a recovery code is never a first factor, and a certificate, a Kerberos ticket, a wallet or a federation partner is never asked for second.
named.name: Name
named.heading: Named profiles
named.noteRanked: A named profile applies, instead of the default, to a sign-in for one of its applications or by a member of one of its groups; where several match, the one with the lowest precedence applies. A realm's named profiles are its own and are not inherited.
named.noteUnranked: A named profile applies, instead of the default, to a page drawn for one of its applications and to a person that application caused to be created. An application is on one named profile at most, so nothing is ranked. A realm's named profiles are its own and are not inherited.
password.heading: Password policy — the default profile
password.lead: What a password set in this realm must look like. It is stored as {dn}, in the shape of draft-behera-ldap-password-policy (the schema OpenLDAP's ppolicy overlay reads), so an ldapsearch finds it and an ldapmodify changes it.
password.stored: This profile is stored at {dn}. Saving replaces it; removing it deletes it, after which the built-in defaults below are in force.
password.builtIn: Nothing is stored yet, so the built-in defaults are in force. Saving this form writes cn=default under ou=passwordPolicies in this realm's directory. A realm created later starts with the same built-in defaults rather than a copy of this one — the profile is not seeded, so it cannot be missing from a realm nobody seeded.
password.checked: Every field is checked before anything is written, and two rules relate fields to each other: a generated password must be at least the minimum length, and at least twice the symbol count plus two — a generator asked for more symbols than that would be drawing for a very long time. A change applies to the NEXT password set in this realm; nothing already stored is re-checked, because a stored password is a hash and there is nothing left to check it against.
password.rulesHeading: What a password must be, right now
password.rules2: and the activation page print them to the person choosing a password, so the page they read and the rule this service applies are one sentence.
password.doors: Every door that sets a password ends in one function in common/credentials.ts, which is what makes the list below complete rather than a list somebody remembered.
password.historyHeading: The history, and what it costs
password.history: A remembered password is the hash it was already stored as, moved into pwdHistory on the person's own entry when the next one replaces it — no new hash is made, and the password itself is never kept. Checking a new password costs one hash comparison per remembered one, about 70ms each on this thread, so a history of {history} is up to {ms}ms at a password change. A generated password skips the comparison, because nothing drawn at random is a previous password. pwdHistory and pwdChangedTime are maintained by this service and an LDAP modify naming either is refused in product mode.
password.generator1: New users created from the console or /admin-api get a generated password by default, shown or returned ONCE. It is drawn by

password.schema: This directory is schemaless, so a container of entries carrying invented attributes says what they mean here. The pwd* names are draft-behera-ldap-password-policy's; the stsPwd* ones are this service's own, because the draft delegates composition rules to the server and defines none.

attributes.heading: Attribute policy — the default profile
attributes.lead: The attributes every person in this realm must hold a value of, and the realm's own custom attributes. uid, cn and sn are always required; tick any other attribute a person here may be given. A person created without a cn is given one made of their given name and surname. A person created before an attribute was required keeps every other door, and nobody's sign-in is refused for it.
attributes.enforced: ENFORCED. This realm is in product mode, so every door that creates a person — this console, /admin-api, SCIM, an LDAP add, a federated first sign-in, the bulk import — refuses one without a required attribute, and an edit may not take one away.
attributes.notEnforced: NOT ENFORCED. This realm is in development mode, where a person may be created with no more than a username. The list is still stored and drawn. Switch the realm with global.mode on
attributes.fromRealm: This realm's own profile is stored at {dn}. Removing it puts this realm back to the default realm's profile, or to the built-in default where the default realm has none.
attributes.fromDefaultRealm: This realm has no profile of its own, and follows the default realm's ({dn}). Saving this form writes this realm's own, which overrides it here and nowhere else.
attributes.builtIn: Nothing is stored, so the built-in default is in force: givenName, sn and mail. Saving this form writes cn=default under ou=attributePolicies. Saved in the DEFAULT realm, it is the policy of every realm that has none of its own.

attributes.customLead: Attributes this realm adds to what a person may be given: each is then editable on a person's page, settable when a person is created, checked against its syntax, and may be required above. They are this realm's own and are not inherited from the default realm. A custom attribute cannot be removed while anybody holds a value of it, or while this realm's profile requires it. At most {max}.
